# Evaluation results

<!-- Generated by eval/report.py from eval/runs/20261112T052616Z/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Retrieval and answer quality of this repository on its own **synthetic** sample vault (21 fictional notes) and a frozen set of 51 labelled questions ([eval/questions.jsonl](eval/questions.jsonl), sources in [eval/DATA_SOURCES.md](eval/DATA_SOURCES.md)). Every number below is read from a committed run folder under `eval/runs/`; values are truncated to three decimals.

Reproduce: `make eval` (runs `python -m eval.run --seed 42`): offline, no API keys, no model download, a socket guard fails the run on any network access. Its wall time is in the run metadata.

## Retrieval (44 answerable questions)

Rankings are scored at note level (chunks collapsed to their note, first appearance wins). recall@k = share of a question's gold notes in the top k, averaged; MRR@10 = 1 / rank of the first gold note within the top 10, else 0. Multi-hop questions have two gold notes, so their recall@1 is at most 0.5. Unanswerable questions are excluded here and scored in the answer section. The exact-key fast path is off so the retrievers themselves are measured. "Provenance" = status filter plus the score multipliers of the provenance layer.

| Configuration | recall@1 | recall@5 | recall@10 | MRR@10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FTS5 only (BM25) | 0.681 | 0.977 | 1.000 | 0.877 |

## Answers and citations (44 answerable, 7 unanswerable)

A deterministic extractive answerer ([eval/answer.py](eval/answer.py)) reads the top 5 chunks of the default configuration (hybrid RRF + provenance), returns the one or two sentences that cover most question terms and cites their notes. It abstains when the retriever flags low confidence or when no sentence covers half of the question's content terms (thresholds fixed before the first run). A rule-based checker scores the answer. The faithfulness number is a **proxy** (token overlap, not entailment); for an extractive answerer that copies sentences it is a sanity check and should be 1.0. No LLM is involved in any number on this page.

| Metric | Value | Definition |
|---|---:|---|
| Answered (answerable questions) | 0.477 | share of answerable questions not abstained on |
| Citation precision | 0.857 | cited notes that are gold notes, over answered questions |
| Citation recall | 0.397 | required citations that were cited, over all answerable (abstain = 0) |
| Citations inside the retrieved set | 1.000 | answers whose every citation is in the top-5 chunks |
| Faithfulness proxy | 1.000 | answer sentences with >= 0.6 token overlap with a cited passage |
| Gold-answer term recall | 0.385 | content terms of the gold answer found in the answer (abstain = 0) |
| Abstained on unanswerable | 0.857 | share of unanswerable questions answered with "no answer" |

## Failure cases

Configuration `hybrid_prov` (the system default: hybrid RRF k=20 + provenance). Explanations come from `eval/failure_notes.json`; entries marked *(auto)* are generated from the run.

### Retrieval: gold note not at rank 1

| Question | Gold | Came back (top 3) | Gold rank | Why |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| `pa-01` | faq-refunds | rb-deploy, faq-refunds, ref-api-rate-limits | 2 | near-tie in fused score: without provenance faq-refunds was first; rb-deploy is newer and more reliable (0.95 vs 0.9), so the multipliers flipped the order ("back" in "money back" matches "roll back") |
| `pa-03` | rb-oncall | adr-009-job-queue, rb-oncall, ref-api-rate-limits | 2 | lexical trap: ADR-009 says workers "acknowledge" jobs; BM25 and the hashing embedder reward the shared word and cannot tell paging from queue semantics |
| `pa-04` | adr-012-auth-tokens | ref-api-rate-limits, rb-backup-retention, ref-glossary | 7 | BM25 alone ranks ADR-012 first, but the hashing embedder misses it ("login credential" shares no words with "access token") and RRF lets chunks found by both lists outscore a chunk found by one |
| `pa-07` | rb-backup-retention | adr-014-vector-store, guide-writing-style, rb-deploy | 6 | pure paraphrase ("how quickly ... lose the main database" vs "recovery time objective"): BM25 has the runbook at rank 9 and the hashing embedder at rank 8, so fusion cannot recover it |
| `pa-08` | team-platform | guide-laptop-setup, team-platform, rb-deploy | 2 | "infrastructure people" matches nothing; without provenance team-platform was first, then freshness flipped the near-tie (the laptop guide was verified about five and a half months after the team charter) |
| `pa-11` | pm-inc-031-login-outage | rb-backup-retention, ref-pricing-2026, adr-012-auth-tokens | >10 | the gold postmortem is archived and the question is not phrased as historical, so the status filter hides it; this is the cost of a hard filter (sf-11, phrased "at the time", finds it at rank 1) |
| `pa-12` | guide-laptop-setup | adr-012-auth-tokens, guide-laptop-setup, adr-009-job-queue | 2 | "access" is shared with ADR-012's "access tokens" and wins both lists; the laptop guide is second |
| `mh-01` | team-platform, adr-009-job-queue | pm-inc-042-queue-backlog, adr-009-job-queue, team-platform | 2 | both gold notes are in the top 3, but the INC-042 postmortem (verified 12 days before the reference date) gets a larger freshness factor than the team charter and takes rank 1 |
| `sf-04` | adr-009-job-queue | pm-inc-042-queue-backlog, adr-009-job-queue, team-platform | 2 | the INC-042 postmortem repeats "job queue" most and was verified eight months after ADR-009; without the status filter the superseded ADR-003 was first, with it ADR-009 comes second |

| `mh-08` | multi-hop | adr-009-job-queue, adr-003-job-queue | adr-009-job-queue | ADR-009's sentence covers "replaced the SQLite job queue"; ADR-003's reasons share no new question term, so no second sentence and no second citation are added |
| `sf-04` | stale-vs-fresh | adr-009-job-queue | pm-inc-042-queue-backlog | retrieval put the INC-042 postmortem first and its backlog sentence repeats "job queue"; the answer is about a backlog, not the technology |
| `sf-07` | stale-vs-fresh | ref-api-rate-limits | ref-glossary, session-2026-10-21-retro | the generic glossary definition ("requests allowed above the steady rate") shares 4 of 6 question terms, the reference page's "burst allowance of 50" only 2; the retro sentence then adds a second, wrong citation |
| `un-06` | unanswerable | (none) | session-2026-10-21-retro | the retro note's "raising the API rate limit" covers 3 of the 4 question terms; only "GraphQL" is missing and term coverage cannot tell a missing qualifier from a missing detail |

## Honest limits

- 21 synthetic notes and 51 questions written by the author of the code, who also chose the provenance defaults while looking at the same vault. This is a reproducible illustration of the mechanism, not a benchmark; the numbers do not transfer to real corpora.
- The offline profile's "dense" side is a feature-hashing embedder: lexical, not semantic. It makes the run deterministic and download-free and is weak on paraphrases by construction. The reranker in the offline profile is a lexical overlap scorer, a stand-in for a cross-encoder.
- The faithfulness metric is a token-overlap proxy. It catches invented sentences and wrong citations, not a sentence that reuses a passage's words to state something false.
- Gold-answer term recall counts content words, so a correct answer phrased differently can score low and a wrong sentence that happens to contain the words can score high.
- One question set, one seed; there are no confidence intervals. With 44 answerable questions one single-gold question moves recall@1 by 1/44.
- An optional LLM-as-judge mode is not implemented; nothing here depends on a hosted model.
